title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Numbers-on-Forehead Communication
authors: Haoyu Wang, Pei Wu, Guangxu Yang
abstract: We give the first exponential quantum advantage in the general interactive three-party Numbers-on-Forehead (NOF) model for a decision problem. Previous separations hold only for restricted protocols like one-way communication for a relation. We construct an explicit partial Boolean function, the Interleaved Unitary Product problem, that requires only $O(\log n)$ NOF quantum communication but $\widetildeΩ(n^{1/32})$ randomized communication. This function builds on the two-party unitary product problem of Arunachalam, Girish, and Lifshitz (TQC 2024).   The main technical obstacle is that discrepancy, the standard lower-bound method for NOF, also lower-bounds quantum communication. We instead develop a regularity-based argument for randomized NOF lower bounds, building on the approach of Kelley, Lovett, and Meka and adapting the regularity decomposition of Abboud, Fischer, Kelley, Lovett, and Meka (STOC 2024) to cylinder intersections. Combined with matrix-product estimates of Arunachalam, Girish, and Lifshitz, this yields our randomized lower bound.
summary: This paper proves an exponential quantum advantage for a specific decision problem (IUP) in the three-party Numbers-on-Forehead communication model. It achieves this by constructing a quantum protocol requiring only logarithmic qubits, while simultaneously proving a significantly higher lower bound for classical communication using advanced regularity methods. This advances the understanding of quantum communication complexity in multi-party settings.
main_problem: To establish the first exponential quantum advantage in the general interactive three-party Numbers-on-Forehead (NOF) model for a decision problem.
main_result: The authors achieve an exponential separation for the Interleaved Unitary Product (IUP) problem, showing an $O(\log n)$ quantum communication requirement versus $\Omega(n^{1/32})$ classical communication.
method: The separation is achieved by combining a quantum upper bound protocol and a novel regularity-based argument for randomized classical lower bounds, adapting advanced decomposition techniques.
model_or_system: The model is the three-party Numbers-on-Forehead (NOF) communication setting, applied to the Interleaved Unitary Product (IUP) problem. The quantum protocol operates in the one-clean-qubit communication model.
key_observables: The communication complexity (qubits vs. bits) required to solve the IUP function, and the expectation values related to unitary products.
important_parameters: The input size $n$, the communication complexity $O(\log n)$ (quantum) vs. $\Omega(n^{1/32})$ (classical), and the dimension $m$ of the underlying matrices.
main_assumptions: The quantum protocol assumes the one-clean-qubit model. The lower bound relies on advanced regularity decomposition techniques and the ability to approximate measurable cylinder intersections.

why_interesting: This work pushes the boundary of quantum communication complexity theory by providing a concrete, exponentially separated advantage in a complex, multi-party setting, which has implications for quantum cryptography and distributed quantum computation.
